newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada tobacco industry to fight anti-tobacco bill.
newsitem.headline: Canada tobacco industry to fight anti-tobacco bill.

text.p: Canada's tobacco industry on Tuesday lashed out at Ottawa's proposed anti-smoking legislation and vowed to challenge it in court if it is passed.
Rob Parker, president of the Canadian Tobacco Manufacturers Council, said the bill, which was introduced to the House of Commons on Monday by Health Minister David Dingwall, was illegal.
"The bill, in its present form, is contemptuous of the Supreme Court ... and is beyond the jurisdiction of parliament as we see it," Parker said.
"If it's passed in that form, I would expect not one, but dozens of challenges," Parker added.
The proposed law would ban most advertising, restrict tobacco sponsorships of cultural and sporting events and give Ottawa the power to regulate the toxic constituents of cigarettes.
Industry analysts have said the true impact of the legislation may not be known until after the bill is passed.
The actual regulations will not be introduced until after the bill becomes law.
The new legislation would introduce fines of up to C$300,000 and jail terms of up to two years for violations.
Dingwall has said that he hopes to speed the bill's passage through parliament, and has urged opposition parties to support his proposal.
Dingwall has even encouraged Canadians to vote against his own ruling Liberal party if the law is not passed before the next federal election, expected by next spring.

However, on Tuesday Parker said the government's intention to fast-track the bill was a violation of parliamentary process. He appealed to the government to allow the tobacco industry time to respond.
The three major players in the Canadian tobacco industry are:
- Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd which controls about 65 per cent of the Canadian cigarette market. B.A.T. Industries Plc of Britain controls 40 per cent of Imasco.
- Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, owned 60 per cent by Rothmans International, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, and 40 per cent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
- RJR MacDonald, wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
